newsitem.title: ZAIRE: China gives investment boost to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: China gives investment boost to Zaire.

text.p: China is prepared to underwrite investment in a joint venture to process copper and cobalt waste in southern Zaire to the tune of $10 million, Zaire's state news agency AZAP reported.

China, which is locked in a diplomatic struggle with Taiwan in various parts of the world, has also agreed to give Zaire 30 million Yuan ($3.6 million) to be spent on a range of projects to be agreed by the two sides, it added.

AZAP said an agreement covering the grant, which follows a 30 million Yuan gift to Zaire's Central African neighbour Congo last month, was signed at a weekend meeting of a Sino-Zairean joint commission.

"The Chinese government is prepare to guarantee investments of up to $10 million that China's national nuclear energy company wants to make through the creation, with (Zairean mining giant) Gecamines of a company for processing copper and cobalt waste in Lubumbashi, it added.
The grant will be spent on projects to be agreed between the two countries.
AZAP said China envisaged cooperation at both government level and between the private sectors in each country.
China, which dismisses Taiwan as a renegade province, has been vying with it for influence and recognition in Africa since many countries there won independence in the 1960s.

China has strong traditional links with both Zaire, where it constructed the parliament building and a sports complex. Officials in Congo, an oil producer and a former French colony, said China's grant was to help boost economic recovery.
Taiwan this month gave Gambia $7.2 million to build a road.
